Of Harold King and Len Fletcher, and in more recent years, Harry Churcher winning the shorter distance road walks; supported by as fine a bunch of sportsmen as ever stepped into racing kit.
Len Fletcher, writing from Lincolnshire, says if you asked for leave for walking, "the beaks of this Fred Karno's outfit would think you wanted to take a W.A.A.F. out." That's a good one, Len!

Or, as our old friend Len Fletcher once said, if you talk of walking—well you are thought to be taking out Blondie in the A.T.S. Len Camin, a football member, regrets he will not be able to do any C.C. running as his team is busy getting points in league and cup games.

Len Fletcher doesn't anticipate race-walking again, due to the effects of synovitis, and living under canvas. In a long letter he recalls his famous tussles with Tommy Green and Co., and hopes to be able to lend a hand on the official side after the war.
Len Fletcher aroused the interest of the locals when he went for a spin on a track in Holland. We regret to learn from Len that his father died recently.
Len Fletcher's welcome return to the road after a long lapse, resulted in him winning a County medal, our other three scoring members filling the first three individual placings.
Len Fletcher, an ex Inter-Counties champion, now making a welcome come-back, walked well to gain third place, and others in our team were, Scamell, Snr., Percy Wright and Don Heath.
True second and Len Fletcher, making a welcome come-back, gaining third place. With three heats in the 220 Yards, the following qualified for the final, G.

The 2 Miles Walk was won by Harry Churcher with Jack Rutland second and Len Fletcher third. Charlie Jones won the Hop, Step and Jump Championship, which was incorporated in the match, and Terry Thompson won the Weight Putt.

Jack Rutland, on returning to the common, then went up into second place, and with McMullen, Joe Coleman, Len Fletcher and Bob Readman not far behind it soon became apparent that, barring a number of accidents, we should add one more to our list of successes.

Len Fletcher's return to the field of racing was very pleasing, his position being identical with that in last year's race. Bert Webb took the prize for the first Belgrave in the scratch race without other award.

Our "B" team once again finished second in the Team Handicap and Len Fletcher, proving he can still show some of them the way round, finished fourteenth and was awarded the prize for the first unplaced member.

Young Dan Godfrey, many will remember his father, who was a walker in Len Fletcher's day, ran a good race in the 440 yards, but was unable to stave off the strong Wallington boy's finish in the last few yards.
Len Fletcher, one of our great walkers from 1925 onwards, is again in West Middlesex Hospital; but it is now hoped that a new course of treatment will bring almost complete recovery.
Regretfully we have to record the death of Len Fletcher, after a long illness, at the early age of 54 years. Our sincere condolences are extended to Mrs.

Len Fletcher and Frank Elson have assisted the Club in seven of these eight wins; Tommy Green six times; Fred Rickards on three occasions; Harold King, Frank Thorn and Ted Saunders each twice; and Joe King and Jack Field once each.

Len Fletcher says that if he asks for leave for walking ``The beaks of this Fred Karno outfit think you want to take a WAAF out''. Flight Sergeant Colin Sutton has hopped from the Middle East to India.
Len Fletcher and Colin Sutton each helped me along the hard road to taking part in what you describe, with great feeling, in your article "The Record Breaker".
